unit.why: A teaching by R. Asher of Karlin on immersion in the mikveh that contains a short narrative: the Maggid of Kozhnitz's son falls dangerously ill, and the Berditchever immerses to change the father's intention in prayer.
unit.boundary_note: narrative embedded in an extended homiletic frame on mikveh

stories.summary_en: R. Asher of Karlin teaches that immersion in a mikveh lets one unite another's mind with one's own, and tells how, when the young son of the Maggid of Kozhnitz was gravely ill and the father resolved to pray joyfully without thinking of him, the Berditchever sensed this and immersed to change the Maggid's intention so that he would pray for the child's recovery, which sweetened the judgments over all Jewish children; further sayings on mikveh follow.
